title: The Voice Behind the Footnote
fact_notes: 登場人物・出来事・観察結果は架空の教材例。実測値・実在資料を主張しない。リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A student named Lena was reading two editions of a fictional novel for a literature project when she noticed an unexpected difference between them.
sentences.ja: レナという生徒は文学の活動で架空の小説の二つの版を読んでいたとき、予想外の違いに気づいた。

sentences.en: Both editions contained the same story, but the newer edition included short footnotes explaining expressions that might be unfamiliar to contemporary readers.
sentences.ja: 両方の版は同じ物語を含んでいたが、新しい版には現代の読者になじみが薄いかもしれない表現を説明する短い脚注があった。

sentences.en: One particular footnote described a character's unusual greeting as a formal expression of respect that was common in the world of the novel.
sentences.ja: ある脚注は人物の変わった挨拶を、小説の世界では一般的な正式の敬意表現と説明していた。

sentences.en: Lena found the explanation helpful because she had originally interpreted the greeting as evidence that the character was being deliberately unfriendly.
sentences.ja: レナはもともと挨拶を人物が意図的に冷たくしている証拠だと解釈していたため、その説明が役立ったと感じた。

sentences.en: However, another footnote told readers that a different character was clearly jealous of his friend, although the novel never directly described his feelings.
sentences.ja: しかし、別の脚注は小説にその感情の直接的な記述がないにもかかわらず、ある別の人物が明らかに友人に嫉妬していると説明していた。

sentences.en: Lena wondered whether this statement provided necessary background information or simply presented the editor's personal interpretation as if it were a fact.
sentences.ja: この記述は必要な背景情報なのか、それとも編集者の個人的解釈を事実であるかのように提示しているだけなのか疑問に思った。

sentences.en: She returned to the relevant passages and discovered that the character's behavior could also be understood as concern about a difficult situation.
sentences.ja: 関連箇所に戻ると、その人物の行動は困難な状況への心配とも理解できることに気づいた。

sentences.en: The explanation in the footnote was possible, but the evidence within the story did not make that explanation the only reasonable reading.
sentences.ja: 脚注の説明はあり得るが、物語内の根拠はその説明を唯一合理的な読み方にはしていなかった。

sentences.en: For her project, Lena prepared a short passage from her own original fictional story together with two different kinds of explanatory notes.
sentences.ja: 活動のため、レナは自作の架空の物語から短い一節を用意し、二種類の説明注を添えた。

sentences.en: One note explained the meaning of an unfamiliar object mentioned in the story without suggesting how the reader should judge the characters.
sentences.ja: 一つは読者が登場人物をどう評価すべきか示唆せず、物語に出てくるなじみのない物の意味を説明した。

sentences.en: The other offered an interpretation of a character's behavior, but Lena clearly identified this suggestion as one possible reading rather than an established fact.
sentences.ja: もう一つは人物の行動の解釈を提示したが、確立した事実ではなく可能な読み方の一つと明示した。

sentences.en: She invited classmates to read the passage and discuss whether the two notes served the same purpose or performed different functions.
sentences.ja: クラスメートに一節を読んで、両方の注が同じ目的に役立つのか、異なる機能を果たすのか議論するよう求めた。

sentences.en: The discussion revealed that some readers welcomed interpretations because they felt uncertain about how to begin analyzing an unfamiliar literary work.
sentences.ja: 議論から、なじみの薄い文学作品の分析をどう始めるか不安なので解釈の提示を歓迎する読者もいることが分かった。

sentences.en: Others preferred to develop their own understanding before learning how another person had interpreted the same words.
sentences.ja: 別の読者は、他者が同じ言葉をどう解釈したか知る前に自分なりの理解を作りたいと思った。

sentences.en: Instead of rejecting either preference, Lena suggested marking different types of commentary so readers could choose when to consult each one.
sentences.ja: どちらかの希望を退けるのではなく、注釈の種類を明示して読者が参照する時期を選べるようにすることを提案した。

sentences.en: She also recognized that readers should be encouraged to compare interpretations with the actual text whenever the meaning of a passage was uncertain.
sentences.ja: 一節の意味が不確かなとき、解釈を実際の本文と比較するよう読者を促すべきだとも認識した。

sentences.en: Lena concluded that an explanatory note is not a neutral addition simply because it appears beside or underneath the main text.
sentences.ja: レナは、説明注は本文の横や下にあるというだけで中立的な追加情報になるわけではないと結論づけた。

sentences.en: The language of an editor can influence which details a reader notices and which possibilities the reader considers worth exploring.
sentences.ja: 編集者の言葉は読者が気づく詳細や探る価値があると考える可能性に影響し得る。

sentences.en: A useful edition can make a literary work more accessible while preserving the distinction between background information and debatable claims about its meaning.
sentences.ja: 有用な版は背景情報と議論の余地がある意味の主張を区別しながら文学作品を読みやすくできる。

sentences.en: For Lena, learning to read carefully now included learning to examine the voices that surrounded the story as well as the story itself.
sentences.ja: レナにとって精読を学ぶことは物語だけでなく、その周囲にある声も調べることを含むようになった。

questions.prompt: What differed between the two editions?
options: The main characters had different names.
The novel ended in two different ways.
The newer one contained explanatory footnotes.
The older one contained a second story.
questions.explanation_ja: 新しい版には脚注があった。

questions.prompt: Why was the greeting note helpful to Lena?
options: It proved every character disliked the greeting.
It corrected a spelling error in the story.
It explained the entire ending in advance.
It supplied context that changed her initial reading.
questions.explanation_ja: 挨拶の背景を知って当初の解釈が変わった。

questions.prompt: Why did Lena question the note about jealousy?
options: The note described an object absent from the novel.
It presented a possible interpretation as though it were certain.
The character had directly admitted jealousy in every scene.
She could not read the note's language.
questions.explanation_ja: 一つの解釈が確定事実のように示された。

questions.prompt: What alternative explanation did Lena find?
options: The character might be concerned about a difficult situation.
The character might be planning to leave the country.
The friend might have written the footnote.
The editor might have invented the greeting.
questions.explanation_ja: 難しい状況を心配している可能性。

questions.prompt: How did Lena distinguish the two notes in her project?
options: She presented both as proven facts.
She removed every explanation of unfamiliar objects.
She hid the notes until all discussion ended.
She labeled the behavioral interpretation as one possible reading.
questions.explanation_ja: 解釈は一つの可能性と明示した。

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of the class discussion?
options: To choose the next novel to publish commercially.
To compare the functions of different types of explanatory notes.
To determine which classmate was best at writing fiction.
To prove all notes should contain the same information.
questions.explanation_ja: 注の種類による働きの違いを検討した。

questions.prompt: Why did some readers welcome interpretations?
options: They wanted to avoid reading the actual passage altogether.
They believed editors could never be mistaken.
They were unsure how to begin analyzing an unfamiliar work.
They preferred notes without any explanation.
questions.explanation_ja: 分析の始め方に不安があった。

questions.prompt: What does consult most nearly mean?
options: Refer to for information.
Remove from a book.
Argue against publicly.
Translate into a new language.
questions.explanation_ja: 情報を得るため参照する。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage say a footnote is not automatically neutral?
options: Notes are always printed in a different language.
An editor's wording can shape what readers consider important.
Every edition contains deliberate errors.
Editors never provide useful background information.
questions.explanation_ja: 編集者の言葉が読者の注意と解釈に影響し得る。

questions.prompt: Which principle best represents the passage?
options: Every literary footnote should be removed.
The newest edition always gives the only correct interpretation.
Readers should accept editors' judgments without comparing the text.
Explanations should distinguish background information from interpretations that readers can examine.
questions.explanation_ja: 背景情報と検討可能な解釈を区別する。

discourse.role_ja: 本文が同じでも注に違いがあること。
有用な注から問題のある注への転換。
読者の希望を否定しない別の方針。
読みやすさと区別の維持を同時に示す。
